# YAML configuration and the Python/C++ API {#sec-ch11}

This chapter describes how a user tells kintera what to compute. A kintera run is configured by one YAML file
that lists the species, the reference state and the reactions; the file is read into C++ options objects, and
those objects build the thermodynamics and kinetics modules of @sec-ch03 and @sec-ch06. The same options objects
and modules are exposed to Python through pybind11, so a Python driver and a C++ driver see one interface. The
chapter covers the YAML input format, the reaction and rate-parameter keys with their defaults, the C++ options
objects, the Python bindings, resource lookup and version handling.

The dependency map of the schemes (a figure) is not drawn yet.

[^rg-cf75c2c1a4cc]: species — list of species maps; required; its order fixes the species index; read by `init_species_from_yaml`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0d9f67f97d841147e23283d2dcdab302238d2c45/src/species.cpp#L148-L155)

[^rg-c14ba67fe94d]: reference-state — map of reference constants (Tref, Pref, use-nasa9-cp, use-h2-cp, h2-cp-mode); unknown keys are refused; checked by `check_reference_state`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0d9f67f97d841147e23283d2dcdab302238d2c45/src/species.cpp#L231-L246)

[^rg-6e6f9ece1710]: reactions — top-level list of reactions, one map per reaction; read by `ArrheniusOptionsImpl::from_yaml` and the other readers; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/kintera/blob/0d9f67f97d841147e23283d2dcdab302238d2c45/src/kinetics/kinetics_options.cpp#L66-L69)
